# METALOGOS

> Metalogos — a language for AI agents where data cannot reach actions it is not cleared for: secret leaks, injection and unauthorized irreversible actions are rejected before the program runs. Compiler + interpreter (tree-walking + bytecode VM) + HTTP server + LLM integration + ML layer (Reflex) + vision (the Vision pillar) + voice (TTS/STT).

> This file is the index for IDE agents and RAG pipelines that were EXPLICITLY pointed at this repository's URL. Not for automatic discovery — the major crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended) do not systematically request `llms.txt`. The value is for tools that were told "read from here" (Cursor/Cline-style integrations, internal RAG pipelines).

## Canonical files

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the methodology for coding AI agents — where the truth lives for each class of question (the source: code, not prose), which mistakes to avoid, what "a naryad is done" means. Read it first, before any task.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): bridge copy of AGENTS.md for Claude-compatible tools (synced byte-for-byte — the drift is refused by the №763 agent-index gate; history: issue #299).
- GEMINI.md: removed as the byte-identical duplicate of CLAUDE.md (the №676 A5 dedup — the manual double-sync of the AGENTS.md bridge copy ended); Gemini-compatible tools read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (the content source) or [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) (the bridge copy).

## Reference and formal specifications

- [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md): the full language reference — §3 Syntax (operators, control constructs, expressions), §4 Built-in Functions (528 builtins, 100% coverage, 0 TODO, SSOT-regenerated from `src/builtins/registry.rs`), §6 the generated index.
- [docs/spec/tools.md](docs/spec/tools.md): the normative tools/abstraction spec (the №645 protocol — every norm probed).
- [docs/limitations.md](docs/limitations.md): the index of the known limitations — the truth lives in the primary sources (ADRs, the sources, the naryad reports).
- [src/grammar.pest](src/grammar.pest): the formal PEG grammar (530+ lines) — the exhaustive specification of the .mlog syntax. It is the compiler's source, not documentation — if it diverges from REFERENCE.md, the grammar is authoritative.
- [tree-sitter-mlog/grammar.js](tree-sitter-mlog/grammar.js): the parallel tree-sitter grammar for the external tools (Zed/Helix/treesitter-index). Not part of the .mlog compilation.

## Examples

- [examples/](examples/): 254 working `.mlog` files covering all the language pillars — the basic syntax (m1-m5), fluid types, control flow, HTTP server + routes, crypto/secrets, cyrillic identifiers, context loading, knowledge graph, hooks lifecycle, schema, skill index, reflex (classification + generation), vision, pattern composition, full apps. Most carry a `.expected` pair (the output) or `.error` (the expected error) — executable documentation.

## Architecture

- [README.md](README.md): the general overview — features, project structure, milestones, roadmap, quickstart, links.
- [docs/PLAN-SUMMARY.md](docs/PLAN-SUMMARY.md): the public digest of the wave plan (a derived artifact, the access mode §16.0-7).
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): the full change history (naryads №1-№843), the SSOT for "what's new".
- [docs/adr/](docs/adr/): 196 ADR (Architecture Decision Records) — every architectural decision with the context, the alternatives and the consequences. The index in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- [docs/threat-model.md](docs/threat-model.md): the single, maintained point about the security limitations.
- [docs/privacy.md](docs/privacy.md): the engineering privacy policy — what data is stored, where, how it is deleted (the CONFIRMED/PARTIAL/ABSENT markers; №519).

## Work orders (naryads)

- [docs/FEATURE_INTAKE.md](docs/FEATURE_INTAKE.md): the tracker for the new-feature requests.
- [docs/AI_USAGE.md](docs/AI_USAGE.md): the disclosure — how generative AI is used in the project's development.
- [docs/MEMORY_ROADMAP.md](docs/MEMORY_ROADMAP.md): the roadmap for the memory system.

## Quickstart

```bash
# Build
cargo build --release

# Check a .mlog file
./target/release/mlog check examples/m1_hello.mlog

# Run
./target/release/mlog run examples/m1_hello.mlog

# REPL
./target/release/mlog repl

# HTTP server
./target/release/mlog serve examples/p7_post_routes.mlog

# Audit (Category A security check)
./target/release/mlog audit examples/p6_full_app.mlog
```
